formation.title: The Manchu Destiny
formation.text:
The scattered Jurchen tribes have been forged into a single nation: the Manchu. From the forests of the Changbai Mountains to the banks of the Songhua, the banners now fly united. But unity raises a question that will define our future: shall we preserve the traditions of our ancestors (the hunt, the horse, the discipline of the niru), or shall we look southward, toward the vast civilization whose wealth and learning beckon from beyond the Willow Palisade? The path we choose now will shape the Manchu for generations.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are riders and warriors: the ancestors guide us.

modifiers.name: Way of the Ancestors
modifiers.text: The Manchu nation preserves its martial heritage and steppe traditions. The Way of the Ancestors demands mastery of riding, archery, and the hunt: the skills that forged an empire from scattered tribes.

options.text: We shall rule from the Dragon Throne itself.

modifiers.name: The Dragon Throne
modifiers.text: The Manchu rulers embrace the mandate of Heaven and the apparatus of Chinese civilization. Adopting bureaucratic governance and scholarly traditions, the empire is administered through the institutions of Confucian statecraft.

advances.name: Manchu Shamanic Traditions
advances.text: The worship of Abka Enduri, the Sky God, and the veneration of ancestral spirits through hereditary shamans binds the Manchu clans together in shared spiritual practice.

advances.name: Aha Retainer System
advances.text: Bonded retainers serve the Manchu noble households, providing a reserve of military labor that can be mobilized in times of war.

advances.name: Sable Fur Trade
advances.text: The forests of Manchuria yield the finest sable pelts in the world, prized by merchants from Beijing to Bukhara.

advances.name: Jurchen Horsemanship
advances.text: From childhood, every Jurchen warrior learns to ride the hardy Manchurian horse across the frozen rivers and dense forests of the homeland.

advances.name: Ginseng Monopoly
advances.text: Wild ginseng from the Changbai Mountains commands extraordinary prices in Chinese markets. The Manchu state controls this trade absolutely.

advances.name: Niru Military Organization
advances.text: The niru system organizes the Manchu people into military-administrative companies of three hundred, forming the foundation of the Banner armies.

event.title: The Niru System
event.text: Our military and civil organization has been transformed through the niru system. Each company of three hundred men serves not merely as a fighting unit but as an administrative district, responsible for taxation, census registration, and labor service. Through the niru, every man in the nation has a role: hunter, farmer, soldier, artisan. The question before us is whether to emphasize the military potential of this organization or its capacity for civil governance.

options.text: The niru exist to put warriors in the field.

modifiers.name: Niru Mobilization
modifiers.text: The niru system places the entire Manchu nation on a war footing, with every company ready to field its three hundred men at a moment's notice.

options.text: The niru shall govern as well as fight.

modifiers.name: Niru Administration
modifiers.text: The niru companies serve as the administrative backbone of the Manchu state, collecting taxes, registering populations, and maintaining order.

advances.name: Border Market Diplomacy
advances.text:
Trade markets at Fushun, Kaiyuan, and other border towns serve as both commercial exchanges and diplomatic meeting points between Jurchen, Mongol, and Chinese merchants. Sable is made up into robes for the buyers of the Ming court.

Available in: Sable Fur Workshop

advances.name: Bayara Imperial Guard
advances.text: The Bayara are the elite of the Banner armies, picked warriors who serve as the personal guard of the Khan, renowned for their ferocity in battle.

advances.name: Baksi Scribes
advances.text: The Jurchen chieftains keep baksi, learned men who write their letters in Mongolian and read Chinese books aloud to them. The court's clerks and translators are drawn from their pupils.

advances.name: Karun Border Watch
advances.text: A network of karun border posts staffed by Banner soldiers monitors the frontier, controlling movement and gathering intelligence.

advances.name: Jianzhou Unification
advances.text: The consolidation of the Jianzhou Jurchen tribes under a single ruling house creates the political foundation from which the Manchu nation emerges.

advances.name: Mongol Banners
advances.text: The Mongols who have joined the Manchu are enrolled in eight banners of their own, beside the eight of the Manchu. Steppe horsemen are entered on the same rolls and drilled under the same captains.

advances.name: Banner Garrisons
advances.text: Permanent Banner garrisons in strategic cities maintain Manchu military readiness while training the next generation of warriors.

advances.name: Willow Palisade
advances.text: The great earthwork barrier of ditches, embankments, and willow trees marks the boundary of the Manchu homeland, controlling migration and defending strategic depth.

event.title: The Willow Palisade
event.text: A great earthwork of ditches, embankments, and willow trees now marks the boundary of the Manchu homeland. The Willow Palisade stretches from Shanhaiguan to the frontier, separating Manchuria from Mongolia and the Chinese settled lands of Liaodong. Karun watchposts monitor the border crossings, controlling the movement of merchants, settlers, and potential enemies. The Palisade preserves the character of our ancestral lands while defending our strategic depth.

advances.name: Hanjun Banner Integration
advances.text: Chinese martial families who defected to the Manchu cause are organized into their own Banner companies, the Hanjun, combining Manchu discipline with Chinese military knowledge.

advances.name: Tribute System
advances.text: The Manchu state inherits and perfects the tribute system, binding vassal states through diplomatic ritual and the exchange of prestige goods.

advances.name: The Seven Grievances
advances.text: Nurhaci's proclamation of the Seven Grievances against the Ming provides a formal casus belli and rallies the Manchu nation to the cause of conquest.

advances.name: Ujen Cooha Heavy Infantry
advances.text: The Ujen Cooha, heavy armored infantry of the Banner armies, combine Manchu martial discipline with the latest military equipment.

advances.name: Kangxi Reforms
advances.text: The long reign of the Kangxi Emperor establishes a model of enlightened absolutism, combining Confucian governance with Manchu military vigor.

advances.name: High Qing
advances.text: The Manchu empire reaches its territorial and demographic zenith: the largest population and one of the greatest land empires the world has ever seen.

event.title: The High Qing
event.text: Under vigorous imperial leadership, the Manchu state has reached its zenith. The realm extends from the Amur River to the jungles of Burma, from the deserts of Turkestan to the island of Taiwan. Population has swelled, granaries overflow, and the treasury is full. Yet this moment of supreme power presents a choice: shall we press outward in the Ten Great Campaigns to pacify every frontier, or consolidate this prosperity and let the empire's wealth become the foundation of lasting stability?

modifiers.name: Ten Great Campaigns
modifiers.text: A series of decisive military campaigns has extended Manchu authority to every corner of the realm, demonstrating the continued martial prowess of the Banner armies.

modifiers.name: Qianlong Prosperity
modifiers.text: The empire enjoys an era of unprecedented prosperity. Population growth, agricultural expansion, and careful fiscal management have created a golden age of abundance.

advances.name: Siku Quanshu
advances.text: The Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, the largest literary compilation in Chinese history, preserves and systematizes the accumulated knowledge of civilization.

advances.name: Canton System
advances.text: Foreign trade is channeled through a single port and the licensed Hong merchants of the Cohong, who stand surety for every ship. State revenue is maximized and contact with the outside world is managed.

advances.name: Village Braves
advances.text: For a hard campaign the provincial officials raise braves, Han volunteers from the villages who are paid while the war lasts and sent home when it ends. The Banners are spared and the treasury pays for no idle men.

advances.name: Jiaqing Reforms
advances.text: On the death of the Qianlong Emperor in 1799 his favourite Heshen is struck down and his fortune confiscated. The road of remonstrance is opened to officials again, the court's expenses are cut and the White Lotus rebellion is put down.

advances.name: Provincial Arsenals
advances.text: In the long Jinchuan war of the 1770s guns are cast in the field and matchlocks made in the provinces, since nothing heavy can be carried from the capital into the mountains. The arsenals are kept after the war to arm the garrisons from local iron.

advances.name: Ten Great Campaigns
advances.text: In 1792 the Qianlong Emperor counts ten complete victories, from Dzungaria to Nepal. The battalions picked and drilled for those wars, musketeers trained to storm the stone towers of Jinchuan, are kept at the capital as the model for the Banners.

advances.name: Manchurian Homeland Defense
advances.text: The ancestral Manchurian homeland is closed to Han settlement and guarded against Russian traders and trappers on the Amur. The generals of Mukden, Jilin and Heilongjiang hold it for the Banners.

advances.name: Statecraft Learning
advances.text: Officials turn from textual study to the practical problems of government. Essays on the grain transport, the salt monopoly, the currency and the frontier are gathered and printed in 1826 as the Collected Writings on Statecraft, and governors try the proposals in their provinces.

destiny.name: The Manchu Destiny
destiny.text: The Manchu nation stands united under the banners. Now the great question must be answered: will we ride outward as conquerors of the steppe, or southward to claim the Dragon Throne of China?

event.title: The Manchu Destiny Unfolds
event.text: With stability restored and the banners flying proudly, the Manchu nation stands ready to write its chapter in history. The foundations have been laid. What remains is the will to build upon them.

destiny.name: Banner Supremacy
destiny.text: Extend Manchu military dominance beyond the homeland. Defeat the Mongol tribes at Buir Nuur and demonstrate that the Banner armies are the supreme force on the northern steppe.

conditions.text: Own Buir Nuur, or a subject owns it

event.title: Banner Supremacy
event.text: The Banner armies have proven themselves against the Mongol horsemen at Buir Nuur. The steppe trembles before the discipline of the Eight Banners, and the tribes that once raided our borders now send envoys bearing tribute. The Way of the Ancestors has been vindicated through conquest.

options.text: The steppe bows to the Banner.

destiny.name: The Northern Khanate
destiny.text: Seize Urga, the sacred heart of Mongolia, and establish Manchu suzerainty over the northern steppe. Build the treasury that sustains a continental empire.

conditions.text: Own Urga, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Northern Khanate
event.text: With Urga in our hands, the Manchu state has become the paramount power of the northern steppe. The question now is how to consolidate this vast domain. Shall we establish horse markets along the frontier to profit from the nomad trade, or garrison the mountain passes to create an impregnable northern defense?

options.text: Open the horse markets to all comers.

modifiers.name: Nomad Horse Markets
modifiers.text: Frontier horse markets channel the wealth of the steppe trade through Manchu-controlled exchanges, enriching the Banner lords while reducing the cost of their cavalry.

options.text: Fortify the passes against all threats.

modifiers.name: Garrison of the Passes
modifiers.text: The mountain passes and river crossings of the northern steppe are fortified and garrisoned, creating an impregnable defensive network monitored by intelligence officers.

destiny.name: Empire of the Steppe
destiny.text: Extend the Manchu banner from Kashgar to Lhasa, conquering the Silk Road oases and the Tibetan plateau. Forge the greatest Inner Asian empire since the Mongols.

conditions.text: Own Kashgar, or a subject owns it
Own Lhasa, or a subject owns it

event.title: Empire of the Steppe
event.text: From the Changbai Mountains to the Pamir, from the frozen Amur to the roof of the world, the Manchu banner flies over the greatest Inner Asian empire since Chinggis Khan. We have conquered peoples the Mongols themselves could not hold. Now we must decide how to wield this power: as restless conquerors forever seeking new horizons, or as eternal guardians of the steppe order we have created.

modifiers.name: The Conqueror's March
modifiers.text: The Banner armies march with the relentless momentum of an avalanche, their supply lines stretching across continents. The price of this endless expansion is the neglect of maritime concerns.

options.text: The Eternal Banner guards what it has won.

modifiers.name: The Eternal Banner
modifiers.text: The Eight Banners stand as the eternal guardians of the steppe order, projecting Manchu authority through swift decisive action and the prestige of invincibility.

destiny.name: The Dragon's Capital
destiny.text: Cross the Willow Palisade and seize Dadu, the ancient capital of northern China. Establish Manchu rule from the seat of the Dragon Throne.

conditions.text: Own Dàdū, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Dragon's Capital
event.text: Dadu has fallen to the Banner armies. The ancient capital of northern China, seat of the Yuan and the Ming before us, now serves the Manchu dynasty. From the Forbidden City, we look out upon a civilization of hundreds of millions. The Dragon Throne is ours.

options.text: We rule from the Dragon Throne.

destiny.name: The Mandate of Heaven
destiny.text: Claim the Mandate of Heaven as Hong Taiji did. The Chahar khans of the steppe are brought under the banners, and with them the seal of the Yuan emperors. Mukden, where the dynasty was proclaimed in 1636, is built up into a capital fit for it.

conditions.text: Own Chahar, or a subject owns it
Shenyang is ours and has been built up to a development of at least 36

event.title: The Mandate of Heaven
event.text: The empire has grown beyond anything our ancestors could have imagined. Institutions flourish, commerce flows through a thousand markets, and the treasury swells with silver. The Mandate of Heaven is not merely claimed but demonstrated through good governance. Yet two philosophies of administration compete for our attention: shall we build a deeper Confucian bureaucracy to bind the empire together, or reform the currency to unleash the power of silver-based trade?

modifiers.name: Confucian Bureaucracy
modifiers.text: A vast apparatus of scholar-officials administers the empire through Confucian principles, binding diverse peoples together under a shared administrative culture.

modifiers.name: Silver Standard
modifiers.text: The empire's economy is reformed around silver currency, stabilizing prices and strengthening trade networks at the cost of reliance on expensive professional soldiers.

destiny.name: The Celestial Empire
destiny.text: Complete the conquest of China by securing Guangzhou and its southern trade, and the rich lands of Jiangnan below the Yangtze. The wealthiest empire in the world is then ours.

conditions.text: Own Guǎngzhōu, or a subject owns it
We or our non-sovereign subjects hold at least 50% of the locations in Jiangnan

event.title: The Celestial Empire
event.text: Guangzhou has been secured, and with it the final jewel of the Chinese trade networks. The Celestial Empire stretches from the forests of Manchuria to the Pearl River Delta, encompassing the wealthiest and most populous civilization on earth. Two visions now present themselves for how this colossus shall engage the wider world: shall we build a navy to project our power across the seas, or turn inward to consolidate this vast dominion into an unshakeable whole?

options.text: Build the fleets of the Celestial Empire.

modifiers.name: Maritime Projection
modifiers.text: The Celestial Empire builds a navy worthy of the world's greatest civilization, projecting power across the seas to protect trade routes and assert sovereignty over coastal waters.

modifiers.name: Imperial Consolidation
modifiers.text: The empire turns inward to perfect its administration. Religious tolerance and military modernization bind the realm together while steady governance reduces the complacency of prosperity.

units.name: Bayara Guard
units.text: The Bayara, 'Valiant Warriors', are the elite guard cavalry of the Manchu Khan, selected from the finest horsemen of the Banner armies.

units.name: Meiren Banner Cavalry
units.text: Heavy cavalry led by meiren-i janggin, Banner regimental commanders, who serve as the shock arm of the Manchu host.

units.name: Ujen Cooha
units.text: The Heavy Infantry of the Banner armies, armored warriors trained in both traditional Manchu combat and modern firearms.

units.name: Aha Retainers
units.text: Bonded servants and retainers of Manchu noble households who serve as light infantry in wartime, valued for their endurance on campaign.

units.name: Village Braves
units.text: Han volunteers raised by provincial officials for one campaign, armed with matchlock, bow and spear. More numerous than the Banners and paid less, and slow to gather from their villages.

units.name: Jianrui Battalion
units.text: The Scaling Ladder Battalion, picked bannermen drilled in the Fragrant Hills to storm the stone towers of Jinchuan. Musketeers trained for the assault, with a heavy train of powder and ladders behind them.

buildings.name: Ginseng Trading Post
buildings.text: A licensed trading station for the processing and sale of wild Manchurian ginseng, one of the most valuable medicinal commodities in East Asia.

buildings.name: Willow Palisade Fort
buildings.text: A fortified section of the Willow Palisade, earthen embankments topped with interlocked willow trees, backed by a deep ditch, defending the Manchu homeland.

buildings.name: Banner Garrison
buildings.text: A permanent military installation housing Banner soldiers and their families, serving as both barracks and administrative center for the surrounding district.

buildings.name: Sable Fur Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop specializing in the curing and processing of sable, marten, and fox pelts from the Manchurian forests for the luxury trade.

buildings.name: Karun Border Post
buildings.text: A frontier watch station manned by Banner cavalry patrols, monitoring border crossings and gathering intelligence on movements beyond the Palisade.

buildings.name: Cohong
buildings.text: The hall of the licensed Hong merchants, through whose hands every cargo of tea, silk and porcelain passes to the foreign ships, and who answer to the customs superintendent for their conduct.

buildings.name: Provincial Arsenal
buildings.text: A workshop under the provincial governor where matchlocks are forged and guns are cast for the garrisons, from iron and coal bought by the state.

buildings.name: Banner Horse Stud
buildings.text: A state-managed breeding facility producing the hardy steppe horses that carry the Banner cavalry across the vast territories of the Manchu empire.

buildings.name: Imperial Examination Hall
buildings.text: A grand hall where candidates sit the imperial civil service examinations, the gateway to official appointment in the vast Qing bureaucracy.

list.name: Offices of the Banner Commanders
list.text: Each of the twenty-four banners, eight Manchu, eight Mongol and eight Han, has a commander who keeps the rolls of its hereditary soldier households: who is born, who is of age to serve, who draws the stipend of silver and rice and who holds banner land. From 1723 the commanders sit in permanent offices in the capital, and the banners answer to the throne and no longer to the princes who once owned them. Rolls that are kept give the dynasty its army and its census at once. Rolls that are neglected fill with absentees who draw pay without service.

list.name: Imperial Household Department
list.text: The Neiwufu, staffed by Aisin-Gioro bondservants (booi) drawn from the upper three banners, ran the inner court parallel to and structurally above the Han Six Boards. It managed the Forbidden City, the imperial workshops, the privy purse, the Yangzhou salt monopoly, and the Canton Hong merchant licensing: a private fisc that bypassed the Ministry of Revenue and answered to the emperor alone. Under Kangxi and Qianlong it grew into the most powerful branch of the metropolitan administration.

list.name: Lifan Yuan
list.text: The Court of Colonial Affairs, established in 1638 and elevated to ministry-rank in 1644, governed the dynasty's non-Han subjects: the Khalkha and Inner Mongolian leagues, Tibet under the Dalai and Panchen Lamas, the Tarim and Zungharian oases conquered in 1759, and the Kyakhta border with Russia. It enforced the Mongol noble register, oversaw lamaist patronage payments, and ran imperial frontier diplomacy entirely outside the Han ministerial structure.

list.name: Grand Council
list.text: The Yongzheng emperor created the Junji Chu in 1729 as a small secret war-council to bypass the Grand Secretariat during the Zungharian campaigns. It grew into the central organ of Qing decision-making: a handful of princes and trusted Han officials reading palace memorials, drafting vermilion-rescript replies, and signing the emperor's will into policy without record in the public archives. Its members held no formal portfolio, only the emperor's confidence.

list.name: Banner Garrisons
list.text: After 1644 the dynasty quartered Eight-Banner garrisons at strategic points across the conquered Ming territory: walled banner-cities (Mancheng) inside Beijing, Xi'an, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Jingzhou, Guangzhou, and the Manchurian heartland. The Zhufang Baqi enforced the dynasty's authority over the Han majority and kept the bannermen socially apart (separate jurisdictions, separate language schools, separate marriage pools) for two and a half centuries.

list.name: Khorchin Marriage Alliance
list.text: The dynastic marriages binding the Aisin-Gioro to the Khorchin and other Eastern Mongolian princely houses, codified in the kheshig of imperial consorts and Mongol princess-out-marriages from Hong Taiji onward. Empress Xiaozhuang, a Khorchin princess, typified the system: every Qing emperor through Qianlong was raised by a Mongol-blood empress dowager, and Mongol noblemen sat in the imperial guard and the Lifan Yuan as kinsmen rather than subjects.
